title: HH-PIM: Dynamic Optimization of Power and Performance with Heterogeneous-Hybrid PIM for Edge AI Devices
problem: Efficient PIM architectures for edge AI devices face trade-offs: traditional PIM reduces data movement but has continuous power demands; hybrid PIM with nonvolatile memory (MRAM/ReRAM) reduces power but has mismatch between fixed computing resources and dynamically changing inference workloads.
motivation: Edge devices have power constraints and limited SRAM/DRAM capacity for large neural network weights; hybrid PIM mitigates some limitations but needs adaptive resource allocation for variable workloads.
method: Heterogeneous-Hybrid PIM (HH-PIM) architecture with two heterogeneous compute modules: (1) high-performance MRAM-SRAM PIM modules, (2) low-power MRAM-SRAM PIM modules. Data placement optimization algorithm dynamically allocates data based on computational demand to maximize energy efficiency while meeting latency constraints.
key_novelty: Heterogeneous-hybrid PIM with dynamic data placement optimization for workload-adaptive energy efficiency on edge AI devices.
contributions: HH-PIM architecture with heterogeneous high-performance and low-power PIM modules
Dynamic data placement optimization algorithm based on computational demand
60.43% average energy savings over conventional PIMs while meeting latency requirements
FPGA prototyping and validation across different PIM architectures
